_readme: Catalogue pages for translation-parity fingerprinting.
WHAT THIS IS, AND WHY IT IS NOT AN EXCEPTIONS LEDGER.
data/translation_parity_exceptions.json exempts one specific EN/locale PAIR
because a real, discussed editorial divergence exists. This file is different:
it classifies a PAGE TYPE whose internal-link list is an inventory of what
exists in that locale rather than translated content. Entries here are
structural facts about the template, not permissions for a page to ship.
THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES.
A pillar index lists the pages that exist in its own locale. EN library/index
carries ~306 content links; its locale siblings carry 7-50. category/index
carries 25; every locale sibling carries 0. That gap is correct - a Danish
library index must not link an English-only page (see CLAUDE.md, 'Locale-native
internal linking'). But the parity fingerprint counts internal content links,
so adding ONE new EN page to its pillar index registered as structural drift
and demanded a locale sibling be touched in the same PR - which would have
meant either linking an English page from a locale catalogue, or filing a
per-page exception. Neither is right, and it fires on essentially every new
EN page, so the gate would have trained people to ignore it.
WHAT CHANGES, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT.
For a page matching a pattern below, the fingerprint's internal-content-link
set is dropped. Everything else is still compared exactly as before -
h2 count, FAQ-schema question count, and .symbol-tile count. So adding a
catalogue entry no longer trips the gate, but adding a real section, a new
FAQ, or a tile block to a pillar index still does, because those ARE
translatable content. Coverage of every non-index page is untouched.
SCOPE. Only pillar INDEX pages - the eight catalogue surfaces and their
locale equivalents. A hub page that happens to link many spokes (e.g.
library/currency-symbols) is NOT a catalogue: its links are editorial
choices that should stay in sync, and it keeps full link-diff coverage.
Adding a pattern here is a structural claim that the page is an inventory.
Raise it before adding one, the same way any other registry in this repo
is treated.
